topic: Running Qwen 27B locally with 4-bit quantization on a single 24 GB GPU using vLLM: what fits, how fast it is, and what you give up compared to the full-precision model
title: Qwen 27B on One GPU

hooks.text: Fit a 27 billion parameter model into one 24GB GPU.
Stop renting cloud GPUs to run Qwen 27B locally.
4-bit quantization makes massive models fit on consumer hardware.
See exactly what you lose when you quantize Qwen 27B.
vLLM lets you serve Qwen 27B on a single card.

scenes.voiceover: Fit a 27 billion parameter model into one 24GB GPU.
scenes.headline: 27B on One GPU
scenes.visual: Close-up of a single RTX 3090/4090 GPU card, highlighting the 24GB VRAM label, with a digital overlay showing 'Qwen 27B' fitting inside the memory bar.
scenes.asset_needed: Screenshot of GPU-Z or nvidia-smi showing 24GB VRAM usage.
scenes.hook_text: Fit a 27 billion parameter model into one 24GB GPU.

scenes.voiceover: Full precision models are too big for your card. But 4-bit quantization compresses the data, letting you run powerful AI locally without cloud costs.
scenes.headline: Quantization Explained
scenes.visual: Split screen: left side shows a large, heavy block labeled 'Full Precision' overflowing a container; right side shows a compressed, lighter block labeled '4-bit' fitting neatly inside the same container.
scenes.asset_needed: Simple animated diagram comparing memory usage of FP16 vs INT4 tensors.

scenes.voiceover: Using vLLM, you load the quantized Qwen 27B. The server starts instantly. You can now generate text directly on your machine, with data staying private.
scenes.headline: vLLM in Action
scenes.visual: A terminal window showing the vLLM startup logs with 'Loading model' and 'Ready' messages. Next to it, a simple chat interface typing a prompt and receiving a response.
scenes.asset_needed: Screen recording of vLLM server startup and a basic API call via curl or Python.

scenes.voiceover: Speed is decent for single-user use. However, compared to full precision, you lose some fine-grained detail in complex reasoning tasks. It’s a trade-off.
scenes.headline: The Trade-off
scenes.visual: A dashboard showing tokens-per-second metrics. Below, a side-by-side comparison of two AI responses to a complex math problem, highlighting a minor error in the quantized version.
scenes.asset_needed: Benchmark results screenshot and a text comparison example.

scenes.voiceover: You get a capable local model that respects your privacy. It’s not perfect, but it fits your hardware and keeps your data on your machine.
scenes.headline: Local Control
scenes.visual: A clean shot of a laptop with a glowing screen, showing a lock icon over the data flow, emphasizing that no data leaves the local network.
scenes.asset_needed: Graphic illustrating local data flow with a lock icon.

reel.central_message: You can run the Qwen 27B model on a single 24GB GPU using 4-bit quantization via vLLM, trading some precision for local accessibility.
reel.audience_benefit: You can now test a large language model locally without needing a multi-GPU server or cloud API keys.
